name: Off Road Adventures at Durhamtown
address: 2350 Randolph Church Rd, Union Point, GA 30669
tracks_on_site: The Bomber pro MX track (1.3+ miles, Mark Barnett design)
PeeWee MX, Armadillo (10 and under) and Stacyc tracks
about 150 miles of one-way trails incl. ~35 miles bike-only single track
flat track and dirt drag strip

soil.notes: Riders consistently describe hard-packed Georgia red clay that can feel like concrete when dry and is hard on tires. The Bomber is a clay/sand mix and MX 1 has noticeable sand and drains well.

layout.notes: Bomber is the flagship: 2+ minute laps with a dragon's back, big ski jump, long whoops and a sand sweeper. Other tracks are smaller, some just wooded loops with jumps. Riders call the tracks tamer and better for families than for serious MX.

conditions.dry: Hard, slick and dusty; ruts rarely form. Bring fresh tires and good goggles.
conditions.wet: A few days of rain makes the clay tackier and much better; riders say quality swings with the weather.
conditions.watering_prep: Bomber gets most of the attention; other tracks prepped inconsistently.
conditions.seasonal: Open daily 9-5 (trails close 4:30); race weekends can close tracks. Youth MX Series and other races on site.

rider_reports.says: Riders describe red clay that gets very hard, few ruts, hard on tires; jump faces hold up but need the right rain. Weekends are crowded and dusty; weekdays recommended.
Rider reports bringing worn tires on a multi-day trip and getting badly hurt on a Bomber double; says the surface is hard and slick.
Riders say after drought the dirt gets like concrete and dusty; rain makes it much better; MX6 and the Bomber are the best when prepped.
Riders say DT has more and better tracks than Highland Park but prep is hit or miss; trails can be torn up by quads and UTVs.
Poster says it is open every day but the MX tracks are not worth the trip for a serious rider.
